title: She Sailed a Wrecked Yacht 1,500 Miles Alone: The Full Case of Tami Oldham
description:
Case 018, the full case file. Tami Oldham, 23, from San Diego, grew up around boats. In 1983 she was sailing the South Pacific with her fiancé, Richard Sharp, a British sailor, when they were hired in Tahiti to sail the yacht Hazana to San Diego for its owners, about 4,000 miles. They left Papeete on 22 September 1983. After about two weeks of easy sailing a storm built to the east and came their way; for three days they tried to outrun it. On 12 October Hurricane Raymond, a category 4 storm, caught them, with waves of forty feet and more. Richard, at the wheel and clipped on, sent her below; she heard him shout, and the yacht was thrown over. She was knocked unconscious for about 27 hours. She woke with a gash on her head in a half-flooded cabin. Both masts were gone. Richard's safety line was still tied on, the ring of his harness torn open; he was lost. The radio was wrecked, the emergency beacon damaged and the engine would not run. She pumped the cabin out by hand, stood up about nine feet of a broken spinnaker pole as a mast and set a storm jib on it. A plane flew low over her without seeing her; later two ships passed too far off. San Diego was out of reach, so she steered for Hawaii, the closest land, about 1,500 miles away: with a sextant she sailed north to 19 degrees and then west, and about a week in she found her watch in the bilge, which let her work out her longitude. She lived on rationed tins, wrote in the log every day and slept with one of his shirts, and she has said she heard Richard's voice urging her on. On 22 November 1983, 41 days after the storm, a Japanese research ship found her just outside the harbour at Hilo, Hawaii, and towed her in. Her head injury left her unable to read for years. In 2002 she told the story in her book Red Sky in Mourning, written with Susea McGearhart, and in 2018 it became the film Adrift. She married, had two children, still sails, and wears a small sextant on a chain. Rook didn't believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story, made with respect for Richard Sharp, who is never shown: before the storm the film shows the yacht and Tami, never a figure in his place. The yachts, the aircraft and the ships are generic low-poly shapes with no names, flags or markings; nobody's likeness is attempted. The charts are drawings with approximate positions, not real charts, and the book on the desk is a plain cover, not the real one. Staging details such as the look of the quay at Papeete and at Hilo, the crates and tins, the radio, the beacon, the cabin, the log book and the lamp, the shirt, the colour of the safety line, the typewriter and the study, the pendant's look, the sloop and everything Rook does are reconstruction, not record. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

authoring.run: scheduled long run, 19 Nov 2026. Rule-picked case was r024-alkemade (oldest upload); a parallel long run claimed it 20 s before this run's claim, so this run took the next: r018-ashcraft.

source_notes: Five of the six pages behind the Short were read again for this run on 19 Nov 2026 through a fetch tool: Wikipedia (W), the RNLI's 2019 interview with her (R), ExplorersWeb (X), Stylist (S) and All That's Interesting (A). Outside failed to load this time (server error); it was read for the Short and is kept in the list, but no fact added here rests on it. Facts the Short already had keep the Short's notes (r018-ashcraft source_notes). Added facts and where they are: From San Diego: W (born there), X ('from San Diego and had grown up around boats'). Grew up around boats: X only (her own background; stated as she tells it). Sailing the South Pacific with her fiance, Richard Sharp, a British sailor: W, R, A (X says newly engaged). Hired in Tahiti to sail Hazana to San Diego for its owners: W and X say hired; X says a couple who owned it; S and A say for a friend. 'For its owners' is used, not who they were. About 4,000 miles: S, A. Left Papeete on 22 September 1983: W, A (S says late October in one line and September in another; not used). About two weeks of easy sailing: X ('for the first two weeks... without major incident'), R ('about 2 weeks in, we were just north of the Equator'); S says three weeks. A storm built to the east and turned their way: R (a depression near Panama that moved west fast). Single-sourced; told only in the general words 'to the east... turns their way'. Three days trying to outrun it: X, S. 12 October, Hurricane Raymond: W, A (S 'Storm Raymond'; X has 9 October for the wind picking up). Category 4: R, S, A. Waves 'forty feet and more': W, S, A say 40 ft, R and X say about 15 m; the line covers both. Wind speeds differ on every page and are not used. Richard at the wheel, clipped on, sent her below: X, S, A (R: she had just gone below and was clipping her harness). His shout 'Oh my God': W, R, X, S, A. Thrown over (capsize or pitchpole: all pages); hurled against the cabin: W, A; head injury: X, S, A. About 27 hours: W, R, A (X says three hours; 27 used, as in the Short). Gash on the head: A, X. Cabin half full of sea: W ('half-flooded'), R. Line still tied on, ring of his harness torn open: R (the D-ring had parted), X (D-ring pried apart); S says the harness was empty. Radio wrecked: W, X. Emergency beacon damaged: R (it did not signal), A. Engine would not run: R, X, S, A. Pumped out by hand: W, R, A. Half of a broken spinnaker pole, about nine feet, as a mast, with a storm jib: W, R ('severed in half', 'about 9-foot'), X, A, S. A plane low overhead that did not see her; two ships: R, X. Order within the 41 days is not given; the film puts them where the Short did. San Diego out of reach with the rig and winds: W. Hawaii the closest land: X, S, A. 1,500 miles: W, R, S, A (X 2,400 km). Latitude by the noon sun; north to 19 degrees, then 'hung a left' west: R (her words), X. Watch found in the bilge about a week in, giving longitude: R, X. Tins, rationed: W (mainly canned food), X (rationed canned goods), S, A. Wrote in the log every day: R, X. Slept with his shirt: R, S. Heard Richard's voice encouraging her: R, X, S, A. 22 November, day 41: W ('On November 22 - 41 days after the dismasting'). Japanese research ship found her near Hilo: X, S, A; towed her in to the breakwater: X (the ship's name, given only by X, is not used). Unable to read for years after the head injury: A (six years), X (took years); 'for years' is used. Red Sky in Mourning, 2002, with Susea McGearhart: W, X. Film Adrift, 2018: W, A, S. Married, two children: W, A. Still sails: X, A. Wears a small sextant pendant: X, A. Kept out: Richard's age (34 or 35), the yacht's length (43 or 44 ft), wind speeds, the owners' names, the ship's name, the Coast Guard, her mother's arrival, what else she ate, the flares, her darkest moment near the end (R, X), and every quote not on two pages except 'Oh my God'.

experiments.learnings: plan/learnings.json asks long-forms for a stronger mid-video reversal and a shorter setup: the setup before the storm was cut to about 28 s (5.0 to 37.2 s) with a new image every 2.3 s; the reversal (the plane that flies on, then the ships) sits in the middle, and a second turn follows at once (San Diego is out of reach; a new plan for Hawaii).

thumbnail: THUMB in scenes.py on the 3D still 'thumb': the dismasted yacht under her one small sail on a grey sea, her at the wheel, left of centre; the hook '41 DAYS / ALONE' on the right over open sky. True to the story (41 days from the storm to Hilo, alone). Checked at 1280x720: the hook is inside the frame and off the yacht and her.

quality_gate.method: One run, five review rounds. Rounds 1 to 3: low-res contact sheets of all 57 3D shots (one frame each) in three parts, plus selected re-renders. Found and fixed: the yacht moored side-on through the quay (now stern-to the quay, sails down alongside); Rook hidden behind the mizzen at Papeete and behind the mainsail on deck; Tami's back to camera at the chart table, the radio and the log (camera moved to the radio side, her turned towards it); Rook's head filling the beacon shot; Rook in front of the tins; Rook hidden behind her at the night helm; the camera behind her head when she hears the shout and at the desk; the Hilo blanket covering her head; the storm cloud reading as black cliffs (lighter, higher, rounder); the alternate angles of the quay, the harbour and the storm deck that hid the characters; the thumbnail hook sitting on the yacht (moved right, over open sky). Round 4: a full-length rehearsal (384x216, 4 samples, 12 fps, every 3D frame, 1,743 frames) composited with captions, labels, overlays, the charts and sound, reviewed as a 4-frames-per-second sheet of the whole video (613 frames). The automated gate failed it on two static stretches (93 to 99 s: the turn west and the sextant close-up; 141 to 144 s: the sloop and the pendant) and the review found the camera swinging into the cabin wall in the pump shot. Fixed with explicit camera orbits on those shots, a whip and a zoom transition, and a near-still camera in the pump shot; the TAHITI label on the charts moved above the caption band. Round 5: the changed shots re-rendered, the composite rebuilt and the gate run again: PASS. 62 shots, mean 2.47 s, longest 3.76 s, Rook acting in 31 of 62 shots (50%), -14.5 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, voice 15.7 dB over the bed, closest match to any earlier episode 0.86 (shot 35 vs r019-adilang-long; the limit is 0.93). Duration 153.4 s. The rehearsal's fingerprint file was not committed; the cloud render runs the real gate at 1280x720 and 60 fps.
quality_gate.checked: Every 3D kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D and the five flat kinds in scenes.SHOTS; HOST lists the 27 kinds in which Rook is placed; no kind is used more than three times and none twice in a row. The first shot is 1.68 s with an impact at 0.03 s. The doubt line is spoken on the wreck. Re-hook at 53.5%. One hush shot (49). On-screen dates, names and figures (PACIFIC OCEAN, 1983; CASE 018; PAPEETE, TAHITI; TAMI OLDHAM, 23; YACHT HAZANA; ABOUT 4,000 MILES; 22 SEPTEMBER 1983; RUNNING FOR 3 DAYS; 12 OCTOBER 1983; HURRICANE RAYMOND; CATEGORY 4; 27 H; ABOUT 9 FEET OF POLE; 2 SHIPS; 1,500 MILES; 19 N; DAY 41; 22 NOVEMBER 1983; HILO, HAWAII; 2002; 2018; 41 DAYS) were checked against the sources. Richard Sharp is never shown; nothing graphic appears (the head wound is one small mark); no flag, name, number or likeness appears on any vessel. The thumbnail was looked at at 1280x720.
quality_gate.not_met: The audio was measured, not listened to. Preview stills at 20% and 80% of every shot were not made with preview3d.py: every shot was looked at on contact sheets, then at four frames a second in the rehearsal at low resolution; the cloud render is the first full-resolution, 60 fps pass. The 13-category score was given from stills and rehearsal sheets, not from playback. Kokoro's reading of 'Papeete', 'Hazana', 'Hilo' and 'Oh my God' could not be heard.

review.weakest: Faces are often three-quarter or profile in the cabin shots (the chart table sits against the hull). The storm cloud wall is a row of grey blobs. Hilo's island is a flat green slope and she is small there. The pendant is tiny on screen. The ship's searchlight frame flashes white at the cut (the transition). Narration and sound were measured, not heard.
